question: What is the meaning of current valuation in relation to value information?
description: Current valuation refers to the current monetary value of an industrial equipment, as stored in the Value information attribute. This dynamic figure reflects the current market value and book value of the equipment, providing a real-time snapshot of its worth.

Figure 6 Information attributes of the main categories “Utilization information” 
The main category of Utilization information has 5 sub-categories. Value information is a dynamic figure 
that stores the current valuation and book value of the industrial equipment. Status information describes 
data of the current and historical condition of the machine storing logs and the warning history. Service 
information stores data about maintenance and service from manuals to service history. Process information 
includes information about the production processes that can be utilized to analyze a machine’s physical 
condition and performance. Machine information contains information about the historical performance and 
energy consumption that can support in a machine’s condition monitoring.  
 
Figure 7 Information attributes of the main categories “Value chain information” and “Sustainability information” 
The main category of Value chain information comprises 4 sub-categories. Customer information includes 
information about previous users and customers including their specific requirements and usage history. 
Origin stores information about the machine’s origin including location of manufacturing. Location contains 
information about the GPS data and the current location of the machine. Compliance describes a class that 
stores information about interfaces and security measures to comply with public regulations. 
The main category of Sustainability information comprises the 3 sub-categories of ecological, social and 
circular information. These sub-categories contain all information that is required to generate a 
comprehensive sustainable picture of the machine.  
5. Conclusion and future research  
The developed content classification of a DPP in the manufacturing industry is a significant step forward in 
order to enable organizations to benefit from the potentials of a digital CE. This paper should be seen as 
opportunity starting a scientific discussion about what information is necessarily required and what is 
optional. The four categories of Product Information, Utilization Information, Value chain Information and

A5. Value proposition and challenges to different stakeholders 
Because of the preliminary nature of passports it is likely that more 
opportunities and challenges will be identified. This Table A7 should be 
considered as a step toward gaining overview on these features. 
Table A7 
Explicit mentioned value proposition and challenges to different stakeholders.  
Stakeholder 
Key opportunities for stakeholder 
Key barriers for stakeholder 
Owner, user and facility 
manager  
• Value increase  
• Expected increased object value because of availability and more 
accurate CE information (Bouwend Nederland, 2020; Chahine, 
2021; Gonçalves et al., 2021; Munaro and Tavares, 2021).  
• Changed view for object valuation (i.e., based on material value 
rather than depreciation of object realization value or market 
value) (Bouwend Nederland, 2020; Hansen et al., 2018).  
• Cost reduction  
• Reduced facility and maintenance costs (Bouwend Nederland, 
2020; Debacker and Manshoven, 2016; Gonçalves et al., 2021; 
Munaro and Tavares, 2021; Riedelsheimer et al., 2020; Rudolphi, 
2018; Stolk, 2019)21.  
• Checking compliance with certification (Gonçalves et al., 2021).  
• Lack of knowledge where to start the renovation, or product repair 
(Zirngibl, J. et al., 2019; Malmgren and M¨otsch Larsson, 2020).  
• There is no clear owner of an object (Damen, 2012).  
• There is no clear responsibility for an owner regarding the circularity 
of an object (Damen, 2012).  
• Lacking incentive and convenience to extend a products life-time 
(Malmgren and M¨otsch Larsson, 2020).  
• The client that constructs the object is often not the object owner in 
later stages of product life cycle (in particular valid for buildings). 
Hence, the benefits are not received by the client who is making the 
costs with exception of long-term projects or leasing constructions 
(Bouwend Nederland, 2020).   
• Additional functionality  
• Informed purchase decision (Adisorn et al., 2021; Munaro and 
Tavares, 2021; Riedelsheimer et al., 2020).  
• Clear overview of options for re-use (Munaro and Tavares, 2021; 
Rudolphi, 2018)  
• Tool for measuring CE objectives to improve performance of an 
object (Hansen et al., 2018; Stolk, 2019).  
• Many government agencies and firms have to procure on the basis 
of CE ambitions. Passports align with these ambitions (Bouwend 
Nederland, 2020).  
• Passport data can support in drafting a renovation strategy 
(Zirngibl, et al., 2019).  
• Detecting structural damage in real time (Shim et al., 2019).  
• Documentation for legal unclarities (Chahine, 2021).  
• Creating informed responsibility of object state (Chahine, 2021).  
Raw material supplier  
• Access to new (CE) markets because of transparent quality 
information of material and object components (Hansen et al., 2018; 
Luscuere, 2017; Munaro and Tavares, 2021).  
• Difficulties to extract material from used products at an equal high 
quality of raw material extraction (Malmgren and M¨otsch Larsson, 
2020). 
Component manufacturer  
• Access to new markets because of quality information of material and 
object components (Hansen et al., 2018; Munaro and Tavares, 2021; 
Smeets et al., 2019).  
• Proposition value of CE-based products (or proper mix between new 
and CE-based products) (Debacker and Manshoven, 2016; Munaro 
and Tavares, 2021).  
• Potential cost reduction (lower testing, reconditioning and fabrication 
costs enabled by technical/usage data) through re-use or remanu­
facturing (Smeets et al., 2019).
